landmarks.name: Bratislava Castle
landmarks.writeup: A historic castle overlooking the capital city, symbolizing Slovakia's rich history and offering panoramic views.

landmarks.name: Spiš Castle
landmarks.writeup: One of the largest castle sites in Central Europe, a UNESCO World Heritage site showcasing medieval architecture.

landmarks.name: Slovak Paradise National Park
landmarks.writeup: Known for its stunning gorges, waterfalls, and hiking trails, it is a popular destination for nature lovers.

landmarks.name: High Tatras
landmarks.writeup: A mountain range offering skiing, hiking, and breathtaking alpine scenery, part of the Carpathian Mountains.

cultural_events.name: Bratislava Music Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual classical music festival featuring international and Slovak artists.

cultural_events.name: Východná Folklore Festival
cultural_events.writeup: The oldest and largest folklore festival in Slovakia, celebrating traditional music, dance, and costumes.

food_writeup: Slovak cuisine features hearty dishes such as bryndzové halušky (potato dumplings with sheep cheese), goulash, and various meat and potato-based meals reflecting Central European influences.
brief_history: Slovakia was part of Great Moravia in the 9th century, later integrated into the Kingdom of Hungary. It became part of Czechoslovakia after World War I and peacefully separated to form an independent nation in 1993.

important_people.name: nudovít Štúr
important_people.description: leader of the Slovak national revival

important_people.name: Andy Warhol
important_people.description: influential pop artist of Slovak descent

current_conflicts: Slovakia is currently not involved in any armed conflicts.
